title: Frontend: Knight Moves
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Knight Moves. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({start=[3,3],occupied=[]}) for an 8x8 geometric knight movement lab. Occupants are {row,col,side:own|opponent}. Render 64 buttons with data-cell="row,col", data-allowed=true/false, and output the count in [data-testid="moves"]. Clicking any square selects it. Own pieces block/exclude destinations, opponents can be captured but stop sliding rays. Pawns move upward, may advance twice only from row 6 through two empty cells, and capture opponents diagonally. King safety, castling, en-passant and promotion are excluded from this bounded geometry exercise.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Generate the eight relative L-shaped offsets, filter to board bounds, and exclude squares occupied by the same side.
alternativeApproaches: Use BFS to compute the minimum knight moves between two squares on an arbitrary board.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Corner; center; same-side target.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
